📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, apple could see iPhone shipments rise 7% next year, giving it a 26% share of global smartphone shipments, according to a new report. Here are the details.

As detailed by AppleInsider, a latest Morgan Stanley research report says Apple is poised to ship approximately 270 million iPhones in 2027, a 7% bump from 2026.

The forecast comes amid a change of pace for Apple, which introduced only the iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo this fall, with the rest of its iPhone lineup reportedly set to arrive early next year.

Morgan Stanley notes that this could push some purchases from late 2026 into 2027, contributing to the projected shipment growth without necessarily reflecting an increase in underlying demand.

The report also comes as Apple and the rest of the smartphone industry continue to grapple with rising memory and storage prices, though previous reports have suggested that Apple is better positioned than many of its competitors to absorb those costs.

Sources indicate that apple raised iPhone prices in September, after keeping them stable for much of the year while competitors had already introduced price hikes. In some cases, they raised prices more than once within a matter of months.

Sources indicate that back to the report, it notes that global smartphone shipments are expected to drop 5% next year, compared with a previous forecast of 3.6% growth. That said, it’s still an improvement over the estimated 13.8% decline in 2026.

When it comes to Apple and the iPhone specifically, Morgan Stanley notes that consumer interest in upgrading has remained largely unchanged year over year, with 37% of iPhone owners saying they are extremely likely to upgrade within the next 12 months. That’s compared with 41% of smartphone owners overall, a figure that dropped by 2 percentage points year over year.

As for the market’s reaction to the iPhone Duo, Morgan Stanley found that 22% of non-iPhone users surveyed expressed interest in switching to Apple’s foldable device, with that figure reaching 34% in China.

Importantly, Morgan Stanley’s survey was conducted after the iPhone Duo was announced, but before it released, so these figures reflect consumer interest rather than actual purchasing behavior.

Apple Intelligence was another factor examined in the survey, with Morgan Stanley concluding that AI features are becoming less vital in driving iPhone upgrades, while factors such as battery life and upgrade eligibility are gaining importance.

Finally, Morgan Stanley found that Apple’s customer retention rate increased three percentage points to a record 93%, while its net switching rate improved to 12%.

Huawei was the only other major smartphone brand to show a positive and improving net switching rate, while Samsung and Google remained relatively neutral, and Xiaomi, Motorola, Honor, Oppo, and Vivo recorded negative rates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in 1966, Gene Roddenberry famously created "Star Trek," and despite the relatively short run of the original series — only 79 episodes over the course of three seasons — the show became a truly groundbreaking cultural phenomenon. For some people, that kind of accomplishment might've been enough for them to call it a day and rest on their laurels for the rest of their careers, but Roddenberry continued to develop sci-fi projects throughout his career, even if none of them ever reached the heights of "Trek.".

Take, for instance, "The Questor Tapes." The initiative for a high-minded sci-fi show following the adventures of an android searching for his own memories and dealing with questions about the nature of humanity never made it past the TV movie pilot that was meant to launch it into its own series, possibly because some elements, including the ending, are just too weird.

Originally airing on January 23, 1974, "The Questor Tapes" starred Robert Foxworth as Questor, a seemingly sentient android created in a lab by scientists working as, you guessed it, Project Questor. Unfortunately, Questor's "memory tapes" were damaged during his creation, leaving him with the robotic equivalent of amnesia.

According to recent reports, searching for his identity and purpose, Questor escapes from the lab and begins searching for his creator, Dr. Emil Vaslovik, essentially kidnapping scientist Jerry Robinson (Mike Farrell) to serve as a sidekick who can interpret humanity for the emotionless, logical robot. The only thing that Questor knows for sure is that he's looking for some kind of boat, and to make matters worse, Questor's on a time limit, as the miniature fusion generator powering his body is going to explode like a nuclear weapon if he doesn't find Vaslovik soon.

As he and Jerry travel the world, Questor has plenty of opportunities to show off his enhanced strength and android abilities, but when they reach the end of the journey, things start to get weird — well, assuming that the opening sequence of an unfinished Questor looking like a half-melted Ken doll twitching to life while strapped down crucifix style wasn't weird enough. It turns out that the boat Questor's looking for is Noah's Ark, and when he and Jerry head to Mt. Ararat to find it, they're instead met with a cave with hundreds of deceased androids laid out on slabs. It turns out that Vaslovik was the most recent in a long line of droids left by extraterrestrial "Masters" to guide and protect humanity without directly interfering. Now, that's Questor's job.

If the idea of a sentient android who never really knew his creator searching for his own humanity sounds a little familiar, it's because that's also a pretty accurate description of Data from "Star Trek: The Next Generation." That's a theme that Roddenberry would return to several times in his career, starting with Spock on the original "Trek" and his struggles balancing his purely logical Vulcan side with his more emotional, half-human heritage, but with Data, the parallels are even more clear.

There's even a scene in "The Questor Tapes" that would be blatantly recycled for "TNG." At one point, Questor and Jerry hit a casino to make some quick cash for their journey, with Questor using his android senses and strength to rack up major wins at the craps table, even reshaping a pair of loaded dice when the house tries to foil his win streak.

Recent findings suggest that in the "TNG" Season 2 episode "The Royale," which involved a lot of rewriting that was created conflict among the staff, Data does the same thing to break the bank at the eponymous hotel. Sadly, he doesn't also copy Questor's tendency to repeatedly refer to throwing dice as "exposing specific faces of the cubes," a bit that's genuinely very funny.

In a recent development, rocky has returned to the big screen amid the 2026 movie schedule, but not in the way fans of the fictional boxer would’ve likely expected. However, the beloved actor accidentally sparked some serious drama after the movie was revealed, and I was totally unaware of it.

Sources indicate that as awards season heats up, the cast and creative team behind I Play Rocky have been making the rounds and promoting the movie. Recent findings suggest that there’s a funny story. So, after he signed off, I noted — we had the discussion [of] should he come on as a producer. I said, ‘Personally, I think you should not. I think it’s going to hurt you. And he agreed with that, and I said, ‘Just separate yourself a little from this.’.

Honestly, the Oscar-winning filmmaker’s rationale (as shared on X) makes a lot of sense. If Stallone were credited as a producer on the film, which reveals him in a mostly positive light, many may be tempted to think he manipulated the narrative. Despite coming to an accord on Stallone needing to “separate” himself from the production, that apparently led to a serious faux pas on the actor’s part:.

The mere thought of getting heat from fans is daunting enough, but receiving heat from a member of the Stallone family is something else entirely. Farrelly went on to say that he later had another chat with the purveyor and lover of the Rocky films, and it went down as follows:.

I called Sylvester [and] I go, ‘What are you doing?!’ He goes, ‘What?’ I said, ‘You said you knew nothing about it.’ He goes, ‘You said to separate myself.’ [I said,] ‘Not that far.’ And he says, ‘Oh okay, I will remember that going forward.’.

The Method-Dressing Madness Behind Mckenna Grace‘s 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Press Tour Looks

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2844 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances.
  • With the newly introduced Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend.
  • In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances. Made a household term by Law Roach and Zendaya, method dressing is when actors wear looks that pay homage to the film or show they’re promoting: See Zendaya’s on-theme looks across red carpets for Dune, Spiderman, and The Odyssey for a slew of examples.

With the newly introduced Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend. A super fan of the Suzanne Collins book series and their film adaptations, Grace—who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner—took a hand in the styling for her press run, weaving easter eggs into every look. Her stylist, Molly Dickson, was up for the challenge of translating Grace’s deep-cut references into custom and archival looks from Monique Lhuillier, Gucci, Celine and more.

In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.

Vanity Fair: How did you get into styling?

According to recent reports, molly Dickson: I went to college in Minnesota and my major was advertising. Two weeks before I graduated, I called my mom and stated, "I'm not into this. I don't wanna do advertising." She said, "Well, what do you wanna do?" I told her, "I wanna do fashion. I wanna go to Upcoming York." She said, "No, absolutely not.".

Right after I graduated, I went to LA, this was 2009 during the recession, and no one was hiring. I got an internship at Marie Claire in New York, and enrolled back into college to get school credit to intern at Hearst. I worked at Marie Claire as a market assistant for almost two years, and then I left and assisted Leslie Fremar for seven years. That's when I fell in love with celebrity. Then ten years ago, I went off on my own.

What would you say are your aesthetic influences as a stylist?

Sources indicate that my personal style relates very similarly to Sadie Sink's style, very effortless. She always wants to be very comfortable and easy, never anything frilly or over the top. Just a simple, beautiful dress, and you let it speak for itself.

Sources indicate that mckenna is a substantial fan of the original film series, so it’s clear you’re pulling from there as influences when dressing her. Is it a collaborative process when coming to one of these referential looks?

She's obviously a very huge fan of the franchise. We actually started having conversations about this tour in April, which is very early to start having conversations. I could just sense her excitement around it. She started sending me mood boards, and I actually looked back today at the mood board and it was, it was a lot of Katniss Everdeen. It had Joanna on it, and it was filled with these really strong female characters from the franchise.

What she really wanted to hit was Katniss’ wedding gown look and the Mockingjay look with the wings. I was really stumped on how to pull that off without making it overly costumey.

It has been revealed that mckenna kept asking, "What's going on with those?" I knew the vision, but I didn't know how to execute it. I was working with Keke Palmer and the designer Michael Ngo. He was making some cool music costumes for Keke, and I asked, "Michael, could you make this silver piece?" 'Cause I really had no idea how to get it done.

In a recent development, he mentioned, “I don't think I can do that. You know what? Just give me a day, let me play around with it." That night, he said, "I figured it out." We got the piece and I thought, "Okay, it needs to be a wedding dress under,” so I reached out to all the bridal houses. I wanted it to be vintage because it would tell a pretty story. Monique [Lhuillier] ended up sending a ton of wedding gowns, and the day before Mckenna came in for the fitting, I actually tried the wedding dresses on myself with the silver piece.

I sent Mckenna five dresses, and the one that she ended up wearing, she said, "That's it. I don't even need to try anything else. That's the one I'm gonna wear." Then, it was a matter of finding the right event to wear it to because it’s pretty nice, very dramatic.

She was in Paris for the Miu Miu show, and I brought it there because she had the Hunger Games Museum event. It was a whole conversation with her team, like, "Is it the right moment? Is it too much for this event?" Her PR said, "No, this is the perfect moment. It's the best way to kick off the tour." The response with the Hunger Games fans—I have never seen anything like it before, ever.

What was the experience of having her be such a big part of the styling process?

It has been revealed that it makes my job so fun because she is so passionate about it and she loves Hunger Games so much, even just finding subtle nods back to the movie. She would say, "I wanna do a ladybug look." Thom Browne did that amazing ladybug dress, I thought, "That's so cool, but it's not really her personal aesthetic." So it’s finding ways to keep it still true to her personal style while maintaining the nods to the film.

The way you seem to understand Mckenna feels something similar to the connection between Katniss and Cinna in The Hunger Games. When pulling looks for her, what comes into play? How do you make her come through and not be lost in the lore of the stories or the dress?

In a recent development, mckenna had said that she maybe wanted to do a red or a dark pink feather look because in the books [Maysilee] gets attacked by the red birds which are like flamingos. I'm pulling in all these red feather dresses and on the runway, this one dress looked amazing. Mckenna said, “That's perfect for the flamingo reference.”.

But we put it on her and it was so massive, and she's so petite so she was just getting swarmed. I said, “Let"s not force it.” The goal was for her to feel comfortable in the look rather than just getting each reference.

The public has been really excited about these looks. Are you thinking about the response to the looks when you’re putting them together?

There's been some conversations in a fitting, like, "Oh, the Hunger Games fans are gonna get this." They're gonna see the inspiration, they're gonna understand it.

But I wouldn't say we're choosing a look because ‘Oh, this is gonna go viral to the Hunger Games community.’ Mckenna is a super fan herself so if she's getting excited about the look, everyone else that's a fan of the franchise is gonna get excited about the look.

Mckenna Grace in Betsey Johnson.

Do you feel any pressure to top the last outfit after each premiere?

Yes. I think it was Paris because that wedding dress did get so much press. In that fitting, it felt like, "We gotta keep our game up high." It's been really fun for my team and market assistants because a lot of the girls that work with me are huge fans of the movie. They're not even seeing it as work. They're like, "Oh my God, this is so exciting. Look at this. This looks like this from the movie.".

What was the inspiration to do method dressing for this press run? What do you think is the value?

Mckenna knew back in April, she remarked, "I wanna do method for this." I personally did not read the books. I'm a visual person, so I've seen all the movies. Lionsgate was able to let me go with the cast when they first saw the movie because my agent was like, "Molly needs to go to the movie to get inspired before this press tour. She can't do a method dressing press tour without seeing the movie.".

Even as the tour was going on, Mckenna kept sending me upcoming references and quotes from the book and stuff like that.

Sources indicate that what made you take it to the next level? From paying homage to not only characters, but the actual actors from the films like Jennifer Lawrence at the 2011 Oscars to even dressing like set pieces from the film.

Sources indicate that that was all Mckenna's vision. On her first mood board, she had a lot of Jennifer Lawrence's red carpet moments because she's such a huge fan of Katniss and Jennifer Lawrence.

In a recent development, with the Rue reference, Mckenna thought that color was just very Hunger Games. It wasn't until she put the dress on, her mom said, "Wait, this is Rue's dress." So that was just fate. I would love to take credit for that.

Why do you think that this styling has generated so much attention?

According to recent reports, I think it’s when you do method dressing for such a major franchise and you really are passionate about it. The thing is that Mckenna is so excited and passionate about this movie. She has said, “I didn't think that I would love doing fittings so much. I used to hate doing fittings.”.

Mckenna Grace in Elisabetta Franchi.

Industry observers note that because every look is so intentionally tied back to Hunger Games and she's such a substantial fan, it's literally like playing dress up with her. I think the fans see it, she's so relatable because she's a fan that all these fans think, "Wow, like, she's a fan and she got to do this." She’s the fangirl living out her dream, and the fans are excited for her that she finally gets to do this.

Recent findings suggest that what do you think are the best kinds of projects to implement method dressing with/works best with? What does it work best with?

Industry observers note that I think the major movies that already have a fan base, like Barbie or Wednesday, Being able to pull inspiration from existing books or films makes it so much easier for a stylist rather than a movie that no one's seen before. There's no curiosity or momentum about it because you're starting from scratch, whereas Hunger Games, Barbie, Wednesday, there's already a level of expectation.

Recent findings suggest that the looks for this press run have been a mix of archival, newly introduced, and custom pieces. How do you make that choice? How crucial is it for you to create an archive for Mckenna?

Sources indicate that it kind of is a mix of what we’re able to source. McKenna really wanted to pay homage to Joanna's character with that scene where she's like, "My stylist is always putting me in trees." She's like, "I wanna do a tree reference." And I'm like, "How in the world am I gonna find a fashion reference that's a tree that's not a costume?".

I love the challenge of sourcing the market, and so do the girls on my team. I think it was 2011 Phoebe Philo where Celine did some tree references in the collection. But just because we find it online doesn't mean that we can get it. So then it's reaching out to every vintage dealer, every rental house, asking, "Do you guys have anything like this?" And they might have it, but they're like, "It's already gone, someone has it." I ended up actually finding the Celine tree dress on the RealReal, and I bought it. I love RealReal.

In a recent development, what is your approach to dressing different clients? For instance, you mentioned Sadie Sink earlier, can you walk me through how that process differs from Mckenna?

Recent findings suggest that it's very different between each girl. I let them set the pace. If they wanna be involved, great. If they just wanna show up to the fitting and not even know what's gonna be there, I try to accommodate whatever direction they wanna go. I have one client that literally last week has sent me over 200 references of dresses that she wants, and another girl that's like, “I really don't care. Whatever you tell me to wear, I'll wear it.”.

Industry observers note that every girl is different, and what makes my job so interesting is that it's not the same. Everyone has very different styles. I think the most key part of a job as a stylist is to keep their style true to them and not just force my style onto them. McKenna's way more girly, Sadie is a little bit more casual, it’s just taking their style and elevating it a little bit.

It has been revealed that will you do any looks inspired by Mckenna’s character Maysilee? The looks have been mostly referential to things and people from past stories. Are there influences of Maysilee in the looks that fans haven't been able to pick up on because the film wasn’t out yet?

In a recent development, in a couple days, she’ll be in Miami for press, and she's wearing a very Maysilee inspired, purple Miu Miu dress that has a white collar. When she wears it, everyone's gonna be like, "Oh, that's Maysilee." She really wanted to have flowers and necklaces because Maysilee is really into jewelry, so it’s very light and flowery.

Can you break down the outfit for the Fresh York City premiere?

Industry observers note that we are doing the Mockingjay dress, the one with the wings, and that was another thing that I was very stumped on. I'm like, "What designer's gonna make these wings?" I had this woman in LA who does wings, she's done Halloween costumes and music videos.

Mckenna Grace in Pamella Roland.

It has been revealed that in the first fitting, I pulled this navy Pamella Roland gown. The fabric is really, really cool. It's like a shimmery kind of organza. I thought, "That's the right color,” but I wanted it to be strapless. I went back to Pamella Roland and they were like, "We can make it in strapless." Mckenna was very keen on having some sort of embellishment to replicate Katniss because she had screen printing on the gown and it kind of looks like wings in a way.

Pamela then drew all these CADs with diamond wings on it, and then we got the wings made. We did the final fitting and I almost started to cry. Her mom's taking videos and it's epic. It's so exciting because the fans were doing polls on what she's gonna wear to the premiere.

It's full circle, we started with the wedding dress, Mckenna did the fire gown, and then we ended with the Mockingjay dress.

What was the hardest look to pull together?

Mckenna Grace in custom Cong Tri.

I think design-wise, it was the fire gown.

Getting the fire printed on the fabric was really hard. I had a while back done a custom Cong Tri gown for Cami Mendes for the Masters of the Universe tour. It was like a gold beaded gown, and I remember I really liked the fabrics that they used for it.

So when I was thinking of who could do this fire gown, I reached out to them first, and I'm like, "Can you guys do something that looks like a fire? Like, she's literally on fire." And they're like, "No. We don't think we can." And again, they were like, "Give us some time." They came back and stated, "We did all these testing on the fabric." I'm like, "Yeah, you did it. You did it.".

Recent findings suggest that what's really funny is we were at a fitting at Mckenna's house with the fire gown in a garment bag, and one of her friends stopped by. It was just a tip of the dress showing and her friend mentioned, "Oh my God, you got a fire gown." Then I thought, "Okay, people are gonna get it.".

Jamie Lee Curtis is marking a rather somber birthday as the only surviving member of her immediate family.

“The long and winding road. Another circle around the sun!” Curtis wrote via Instagram on Sunday, November 22, marking her 68th birthday. “Today will be the first year that I am the only surviving family member of my immediate family and my immediate second family. The last in the line.”.

Recent findings suggest that curtis’ older sister, Kelly Lee Curtis, died earlier this year of natural causes, according to the Blaine County coroner’s office. She was in hospice care for the week prior to her death. She was 69.

Industry observers note that “A warm aloha to my older sister, Kelly Lee Curtis. She passed away this morning. In her home. In nature. At peace,” Jamie Lee wrote via Instagram at the time, announcing her sister’s death. “She was my first friend and lifelong confidant. She was jaw droppingly beautiful, and a talented actress.”.

On Saturday, Jamie Lee opened up about how the loss of her sister is impacting her on her birthday.

Recent findings suggest that “The loss of my sister Kelly in June was a real blow and I feel sad today,” Jamie Lee continued in her Saturday post. “I look back at photographs of me as a child, and I look so stunned to be here at birth, and it carried on through much of my young life, always seemingly startled and slightly concerned. I’ve worked through a lot of that discomfort, and I’m so happy to be here and have the life I have. Both personal and creative.”.

She added, “What remains for me is the legacy of other humans who forged a path for me to be here through their actions and examples as I hope I am for my own family and of course friends and, as a public person, the millions of people I’ve involved in my life.”.

Jamie Lee’s daughter, Janet Leigh, died in 2004 at age 77 at her Beverly Hills home following a struggle with vasculitis. Her father, Tony Curtis, died in 2010 at age 85 from cardiac arrest at his home in Nevada.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 may be the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic, and may have earned a record-breaking $3.79 billion on launch day, but that doesn't mean Rockstar Games' new blockbuster can't have its haters. Multiple groups have descended on GTA 6's Metacritic page to attack the game for its perceived shortcomings, much of that criticism is based on culture war nonsense.

But some of GTA 6's detractors are targeting the game for another reason: for slighting The Legend of Zelda.

In a recent development, GTA 6 made its debut on Metacritic with a 99 Metascore, based on more than 150 critics reviews. That feat nudged the previous best game of all time, at least going by Metacritic score averages, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, down to No. 2 on the review aggregator website. That has led some Legend of Zelda supporters to review bomb Grand Theft Auto 6 on Metacritic, and some GTA 6 supporters to do the same to Zelda. Now, both camps are in a pointless war to lower the other franchise's user review score.

Over the past few days, GTA and Zelda fans have been trading barbs and slinging "0" user review scores at their perceived rivals. As of Sunday, Nov. 22, Grand Theft Auto 6's user review score on Metacritic has dipped to 5.6, indicating "mixed or average" reviews from players. In response, the original Ocarina of Time and its Nintendo Switch 2 remake have also been review bombed (though their user scores are in the mid-8s as of Sunday).

Unsurprisingly, the discourse around this pointless feud has not been particularly intelligent. Each camp is simply trying to drive down its rivals’ user score, with supporters writing the bare minimum in their user "reviews" — often with plenty of typos.

In a recent development, even poor Soulcalibur, the 1999 fighting game released on Dreamcast, is catching strays amid the fighting. Some GTA 6 supporters are now wading into Soulcalibur's user reviews, slamming Bandai Namco's weapons-based fighter for no good reason beyond its ranking as the third-best game of all time according to Metacritic's algorithm.

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto 6's detractors aren't just misguided Zelda fans. Unsurprisingly, a contingent of GTA fans are attacking the game for its perceived "wokeness" amid more legitimate concerns about performance. "30 FPS, Concole Exclusive, Restricted freedom and uninteresting characters are a no go for a 13 year development cycle," reads one recent negative review of GTA 6. Much of the feedback, however, seems to focus on having a female co-lead character and game mechanics that ask players to be considerate toward her.

"In GTA6 you need to do chores, pick up an abusive girl from prison and then do more chores. Boring characters, boring missions and 30fps cap. I would have rather burned that $100 than giving it to the woke garbage R* has become," reads one scathing review.

"15 years for this dissapointing cuck simulator. Rip rockstar. You were my childhood," reads another. "Game is straight woke trash," another troll says.

The tenor of GTA 6's negative reviews isn't much different from the trollish feedback infesting reviews of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, surprisingly. "THEY MADE LINK A CUCK IN THIS GAME!!!!! ALWAYS DOING WHAT HIS FEMALE FAIRY NAVI TELLS HIM WHAT TO DO!!!! CRITICS PROVE ONCE AGAIN THEY’VE BEEN BOUGHT OFF!!!!!" reads one of the many negative reviews to invoke cuck simulator language.

It has been revealed that while this kind of petty squabbling is par for the course in internet discourse, especially in the video game sphere, at least fans of both The Legend of Zelda and Grand Theft Auto can take comfort in knowing that both franchises have great games to enjoy in 2026. And that, if you're reading this, you're likely not spending your time fighting in the Metacritic comments.

#74203. All 10 James Bond Movies Not Based On Ian Fleming's Books, Ranked

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2085 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Slashfilm ↗ Open Full Page

All 10 James Bond Movies Not Based On Ian Fleming's Books, Ranked

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2085 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that we're taking a look back at the James Bond movies that are not based on Ian Fleming's books and short stories.
  • Here are all 10 James Bond movies not based on Ian Fleming's books ranked, going in their own direction with the super-spy.
  • Sources indicate that pierce Brosnan at the moment remains the only actor whose entire run as James Bond featured original narratives for his movies, rather than drawing directly from a specific Fleming story.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that we're taking a look back at the James Bond movies that are not based on Ian Fleming's books and short stories. Some of the entries here take their titles from short stories written by Ian Fleming but, frankly, nothing else. Outside of the inclusion of Bond and his usual allies and enemies, these cinematic narratives really strike out on their own creatively.

Here are all 10 James Bond movies not based on Ian Fleming's books ranked, going in their own direction with the super-spy.

Sources indicate that pierce Brosnan at the moment remains the only actor whose entire run as James Bond featured original narratives for his movies, rather than drawing directly from a specific Fleming story. In taking Bond out of the Cold War setting in which he originated, this led to an uneven tenure, despite Brosnan's best efforts. However, nothing could quite save Brosnan's last turn as 007 in 2002's "Die Another Day," opening with a title track by Madonna that sounded dated when it was released. The movie has Bond square off with a rogue North Korean general while trying to identify who betrayed him on a mission that led to a prolonged torturous imprisonment.

In a recent development, IMDb names "Die Another Day" as the worst James Bond movie, a dubious distinction that is, unfortunately, well-deserved. The movie opens with Bond infiltrating North Korea by surfing, because that's clearly what the kids are still into, and it only gets worse from there. This backslide into mediocrity spreads to the cinematography, complete with shoddy CG effects and random slow-motion sequences for no discernible reason other than an attempt to look cool. An absolute travesty and an embarrassing way for Brosnan to end his time as Bond, "Die Another Day" is a grating viewing experience.

According to recent reports, yes, "A View to a Kill," Moore's swan song to the franchise, takes its title from the 1960 Fleming short story "From a View to a Kill." But whereas the literary namesake features Bond hunting a motorcycle-driving assassin in France, the 1985 movie pits 007 against an immoral tech tycoon before it was cool. The tycoon in question is Max Zorin (Christopher Walken), a sadistic figure looking to corner the microchip market by destroying Silicon Valley. But outside of Walken chewing the scenery, joined by Grace Jones playing his enforcer, and a memorable title track by Duran Duran, the movie falls flat.

Roger Moore was horrified by "A View to a Kill," particularly the widespread casual violence, as Zorin mercilessly murders many of his associates. We're personally horrified by how rough around the edges the overall movie is, from its lackluster stunts to its abrupt finale. To make matters worse, when the movie's filming wrapped, at 57 years old, Moore looks visibly aged out of playing a spry secret agent. A half-hearted end to Moore's celebrated run playing James Bond, "A View to a Kill" feels as tired as its lead actor.

It has been revealed that daniel Craig's sophomore outing as Bond in 2008's "Quantum of Solace" also takes its title from a 1960 short story written by Fleming. But the literary tale simply follows Bond as he attends a dinner party in Nassau where he hears a story about an unhappy marriage. With that certainly not enough for an action movie to go off of, the film instead functions as a direct sequel to "Casino Royale," opening minutes later. Bond uncovers a global network that's infiltrated government organizations worldwide, including MI6, while contending with his own unresolved grief over his recently deceased lover Vesper Lynd (Eva Green).

For as much grief as "Quantum of Solace" gets, constantly existing in the shadow of "Casino Royale," it's a perfectly watchable Bond movie. The shortest in the series to date, the film does feel like a parade of action set pieces, but Craig's performance grounds the spectacle. The movie's themes about water scarcity and a cabal of affluent influencers trying to manipulate international governments does feel prescient. Coming off as an extended epilogue to "Casino Royale" rather than its own standalone experience, "Quantum of Solace" really works best watched in concert with its immediate predecessor.

Compared to its more action-oriented predecessor, "The World Is Not Enough" tried to lean more into dramatic territory. The 1999 movie opens with Bond (Brosnan) tricked into delivering a bomb to MI6 related to a kidnapping plot involving oil heiress Elektra King (Sophie Marceau). After being assigned to protect Elektra, Bond hunts down the terrorist responsible for the explosive incident, only to uncover a whole plot targeting vital oil pipelines into Europe. This leads Bond to realize that Elektra is not as helpless or innocent as he believed when they struck up their illicit romance.

It has been revealed that taking its title from Bond's family motto introduced in "On Her Majesty's Secret Service," "The World Is Not Enough" tries to feel like a more personal adventure for 007 accordingly. But as good a femme fatale as Sophie Marceau is, the movie never quite delivers on the emotional potential that it aspires to. The action is a bit lackluster too, feeling like something more akin to a theme park stunt spectacular than a blockbuster set piece. Underscoring that Brosnan was often working with lesser material during his Bond run, "The World Is Not Enough" couldn't live up to its creative ambitions.

There was a lot of expectation riding on "Spectre" after the critical and commercial success of its immediate predecessor "Skyfall." The movie also marks the first official Bond movie since "Diamonds Are Forever" to explicitly include Ernst Stavro Blofeld, after protracted legal challenges prevented the villain's usage. This time, Blofeld is played by Christoph Waltz, with the added backstory that he and Bond grew up together contentiously as surrogate brothers, before the criminal mastermind faked his death. Since then, the movie reveals Blofeld has secretly been tormenting Bond from the shadows, leading to their eventual unhappy reunion for the fate of the world.

In a recent development, "Spectre" falls into the trap of trying to emulate "Skyfall" too much, right down to directly lifting music tracks from the preceding movie's score. The idea of Blofeld being Bond's brother figure, a concept also introduced in the 007 spoof "Austin Powers in Goldmember," is a laughable way to make their dynamic feel more personal. What salvages the movie from its lackluster script is its top-notch cinematography by Hoyte van Hoytema, particularly its stunning opening scene in Mexico City.

Brosnan's sophomore outing as Bond in 1997's "Tomorrow Never Dies" doesn't get as much credit as it deserves, overshadowed by its more successful predecessor. Another prescient entry in the series as far as its story is concerned, the main villain is a murderous media mogul providing his own news output. In order to take his media empire to the next level, Elliot Carver (Jonathan Pryce) tries to orchestrate a war between the United Kingdom and China. Bond and Chinese intelligence operative Wai Lin (Michelle Yeoh) work together to expose Carver's plot and prevent the conflict from breaking out.

Considering "Tomorrow Never Dies" scrapped its script days before filming, it's a wonder the movie came out as well as it did. The movie goes even more global than many other series' entries, taking Bond everywhere from Carver's offices in Germany to the streets of Saigon. What holds the movie back is that its plot does feel visibly rushed, while none of the action set pieces are as satisfying as the big moments in "GoldenEye." A glossier approach to the franchise than its predecessor's post-Cold War grittiness, "Tomorrow Never Dies" is a serviceable entry in Brosnan's Bond legacy.

Recent findings suggest that when Daniel Craig closed out his celebrated run as James Bond, he did so with a bang, leaving no stone unturned. This made "No Time to Die" the longest James Bond movie ever, opening with Bond believing his latest serious paramour, Madeleine Swann (Léa Seydoux), had betrayed him to Spectre. After abruptly leaving the service in the wake of this assumption, Bond is pulled back into action when a secret weapon is stolen from the British government. In the process of destroying this deadly project, Bond has to face familiar faces from his life before a fatal showdown against the terrorist Lyutsifer Safin (Rami Malek).

While it could've trimmed about 15 minutes from its runtime, "No Time to Die" provides Craig with a largely solid farewell. From the dusty streets of Italy where Bond tries to get closure for the events of "Casino Royale" to its explosive finale, the movie hits all the right notes. The film's villains, including Malek's Safin, are a bit of a mixed bag, but the action, including a centerpiece sequence in Cuba, is competently staged. A satisfying end to Craig's five-movie run as 007, "No Time to Die" sticks the landing even if it takes some time to get there.

While it's not as fondly remembered today, 1989's "License to Kill" is an essential James Bond everyone should see at least once. Timothy Dalton's second and final turn as 007, the movie begins with Felix Leiter (David Hedison) and his new bride being attacked by drug lord Franz Sanchez (Robert Davi). With MI6 refusing to retaliate, considering the incident an outside matter, Bond angrily resigns from the service and sets out to avenge his friend. This unsanctioned vendetta eventually reveals that there is more at stake with Sanchez's latest scheme than Bond realized.

Though Dalton brought a more serious edge to Bond with his first movie in the role, "The Living Daylights," "License to Kill" is where he really cuts loose. Long before Daniel Craig did it, Dalton played Bond as a mean, lethal type that had no problem with getting his hands dirty to get the job done. These harder-edged sensibilities caught people off-guard, with the memory of the light-hearted Roger Moore tenure still fresh in their minds. But if you're looking to see why Timothy Dalton is filmmaker Christopher Nolan's favorite Bond actor, "License to Kill" is the perfect showcase.

It has been revealed that after a six-year hiatus following "License to Kill," James Bond finally returned to the silver screen in 1995, this time with Pierce Brosnan playing the role. "GoldenEye" was almost the end of the James Bond franchise as it tried to find its way after the Cold War. The specter of those global tensions certainly inform the movie's story, with Bond learning a Soviet-era weapons satellite has been hijacked. Venturing into the heart of Russia to identify the culprit, Bond comes face-to-face with his old friend and former 00 Agent Alec Trevelyan (Sean Bean), now leading a crime syndicate.

Industry observers note that the Bond movie series needed a shot of adrenaline if it hoped to stay alive after the Cold War, and "GoldenEye" delivered. Brosnan strikes the perfect balance between Moore's self-aware charm and Dalton's steely-eyed intensity while exploring the nuances of the character like never before. The action is as memorable as the franchise gets, and the supporting cast around Brosnan all turn in fantastic work, especially Bean as Trevelyan. Cementing the franchise's relevance beyond a set time period, "GoldenEye" remains the most crucial box office hit in Bond history, and that comes from a film of enduring quality.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of box office success, "Skyfall" became the biggest James Bond movie ever when it opened in theaters in 2012. Continuing Daniel Craig's run after a four-year hiatus, the movie has Bond reconcile with his lethal occupation's toll on his body and mind after a disastrous mission in Istanbul. Returning to duty after London is attacked by a shadowy figure linked to M (Judi Dench) and her own unresolved legacy, Bond has to contend with his own advancing age. Fortunately, this mission and its eccentric villain Raoul Silva (Javier Bardem) are just the things to help Bond overcome his midlife crisis.

Sources indicate that released in time for the film series' 50th anniversary, "Skyfall" feels like a celebration and commentary on the legacy of James Bond. Under sharp direction from Sam Mendes, the movie beautifully illustrates those themes while delivering bombastic action sequences, including a fantastic fight scene in Shanghai. Elevating the proceedings is haunting cinematography from Roger Deakins, really accentuating the light and shadows that Bond frequently plays in. An absolute masterpiece from top to bottom, "Skyfall" deconstructs Bond and thematically rebuilds him for the 21st century.

  • It has been revealed that 9-1-1 has officially wrapped up the first half of its 10th season on the 2026 TV schedule, and it was anything but calm.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that warning! Spoilers ahead for the Season 10 fall finale of 9-1-1, “Et Tu?,” which is available to stream with a Hulu subscription.

It has been revealed that 9-1-1 has officially wrapped up the first half of its 10th season on the 2026 TV schedule, and it was anything but calm. Thursday’s fall finale included some intense calls, and even more intense scenes between Buck and Eddie as their latest fallout continues. The best friends have not really been on the same page for a while now, and I’ve been worried about them. Luckily, the executive producer is explaining where things stand with them following the midseason finale.

It has been revealed that buck’s substantial decision in the Season 9 finale to foster his biological son following the death of his parents has led to some difficulties at the start of Season 10. The toddler, Theo, is a bit rambunctious and doesn’t take well to authority. This has put a strain on Buck’s relationship with Eddie, who knows what it’s like to be a single father. It doesn’t help that after Buck decided to give Theo up, Eddie became his foster dad through emergency placement. This has put even more pressure on them, and EP and showrunner Tim Minear told TV Insider why they went in this direction:.

Sources indicate that I think conflict is drama, obviously, but it felt… To me, it was sort of an interesting way to have Eddie come in and take Buck’s story away from him in a sense. They both have stories, right? Obviously, Theo is Buck’s biological kid. Buck had every good intention of fostering and growing into that role, which he still has an opportunity to do. But also, I just believe that Eddie would not let that kid go into a group home. And I think there was some truth in what Buck noted about Eddie’s guilt about being ambivalent about his own son in the first five years of his life.

Buck had donated sperm to his friend and his wife, who were having trouble conceiving a few seasons ago, and after helping her deliver, it didn’t really come up again...until last season. Then, after the couple died in a car crash, Buck felt responsible for the kid and took him in. There was some concern for Buck going into Season 10, and it was obvious this wasn’t going to be easy, especially after seeing Theo’s chaotic energy. So he ultimately believed that Theo would be better with someone else.

However, Minear is right in believing that Eddie, who was the only one who knew what Buck was doing, wouldn’t let Theo go to a group home. Unfortunately, this creates more conflict between them, but it’s what makes the situation more realistic:.

So again, a lot of the stories here this season — look, we’re in Season 10, and a lot of the stories this season are an accumulation of canon that we’ve built up over the past decade with these characters. And that always makes for a richer story, it seems to me. But I actually think Buck and Eddie, conflict is natural, particularly between people who are really close. Nobody can piss you off as much as someone who you’re really close to, and I just think that’s real.

Despite the growing tension in the midseason finale, Buck and Eddie had somewhat made up towards the end of the episode. While Buck wasn’t quite ready to see Theo, he understood why Eddie did what he did. It’s hard to tell where things will go for them in the upcoming year, but with Theo staying with Eddie and Buck coming to terms with everything, it should be interesting. On that note, Minear shares that both of them will have some growing to do for multiple reasons:.

Yeah, I think they’re at an interstitial stage where Buck sees that it is really best for Theo right now to be with Eddie. Maybe neither one of them handled it perfectly, but if they handled it perfectly, then you’d have a five-episode season as opposed to 18. But I think they’re in a good place in their friendship. I think that Theo becomes a spoiler a little bit, and until Buck feels like he can walk into that house and face that kid, there’s kind of a natural barrier there between whatever kind of closeness that he can enjoy with Eddie off the job.

Sources indicate that I have been worried about Buck and Eddie’s relationship since the beginning of the season, when it was clear that Buck fostering Theo would bring some problems. And it didn’t get any easier when Eddie became the foster parent. I’m definitely glad that they’ve crossed a barrier, and they both realize how they acted in this situation might not have been the best. However, I am looking forward to seeing what happens now that they have an understanding with each other and Theo.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

9-1-1 is now on its winter hiatus, but the series will return on Thursday, January 7 at 8 p.m. ET on ABC, streaming the next day on Hulu.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • “Cancer does change you,” Kate Middleton says, emotion clear in her voice.
  • According to Kensington Palace, which unveiled the film on Saturday, Heal is “a deeply personal new documentary from The Princess of Wales, exploring life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.” It will air on the BBC in the UK on November 29, and in the US on NBCUniversal on November 30.
  • Heal follows Kate Middleton during her participation in one of the United Kingdom’s most demanding endurance events: The National Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed this summer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“Cancer does change you,” Kate Middleton says, emotion clear in her voice. “It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.” These words come not at as an Instagram post or at a public event. Instead, they're the voice-over in a previously unannounced documentary about the Princess of Wales and her life since she disclosed a diagnosis of cancer in 2024.

According to Kensington Palace, which unveiled the film on Saturday, Heal is “a deeply personal new documentary from The Princess of Wales, exploring life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.” It will air on the BBC in the UK on November 29, and in the US on NBCUniversal on November 30.

Heal follows Kate Middleton during her participation in one of the United Kingdom’s most demanding endurance events: The National Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed this summer. In less than 24 hours, the princess climbed the three highest mountains in Scotland, England, and Wales: Ben Nevis (4,413 feet), Scafell Pike (3,209 feet), and Yr Wyddfa–Snowdon (3,559 feet). The undertaking wasn't just a personal effort, as it was also in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, an organization that supports people living with cancer before, during, and after the disease.

The documentary will also support that organization, Kensington Palace notes, saying “All funds received through the documentary's distribution have been directed to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity to help people living with and beyond cancer.” The Royal Marsden Hospital, at which Middleton received treatment, is also referenced in the film, as Middleton's brother, James, asks her “Isn’t it when you leave the Royal Marsden, you ring the bell?”.

But while many patients participate in the bell-ringing ritual at the conclusion of treatment, Middleton says she missed out on that moment. “Yeah, but I didn’t ring the bell,” she replies. “So maybe this is your ringing of the bell,” James responded, suggesting her Three Peaks experience was that symbolic peal.

While Prince William is no stranger to documentary work, nor are Prince Harry and wife Meghan Markle, this is Kate Middleton's first venture into the format. Perhaps to ease her into the project, Heal's Director of Photography is a face quite familiar to the Princess: Will Warr, the filmmaker behind her video announcement marking the end of her chemotherapy treatments.

Recent findings suggest that “Through this documentary, The Princess hopes to help others navigate diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer and transform access to holistic cancer care which supports wellbeing, resilience and quality of life during and after diagnosis,” Kensington Palace notes of Heal, a message underscored by Middleton's words in the trailer. “You know, healing is a journey. How to reconnect with the things you once knew and how to find a sense of hope and joy alongside uncertainty.”.

“It’s clear we're not meant to face life’s challenges alone,” the princess says as the trailer concludes. “Things can renew and grow. Often it is through pain that we realize that there is a greater beauty that lies beyond that.".

Robert Pattinson's Divisive Sci-Fi Action Movie Proves He's Perfect For James Bond

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The proof is in Christopher Nolan's 2020 time-warp thriller "Tenet," wherein Pattinson sports a dazzling wardrobe of bespoke suits, knit polos, scarves, and impeccably rumpled pocket squares.
  • And, as we all know, looking good in a suit is one of the main requirements to play 007, so Pattinson has already passed his first test as our newly-cast James Bond.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that how good does Robert Pattinson look in a tailored suit? Damn good, is the answer.

The proof is in Christopher Nolan's 2020 time-warp thriller "Tenet," wherein Pattinson sports a dazzling wardrobe of bespoke suits, knit polos, scarves, and impeccably rumpled pocket squares. The attire in "Tenet," provided by Oscar-nominated costume designer Jeffrey Kurland, are so impressive that GQ Magazine had to pause to write an article about them (even if it was just to complain that the suits look a little too good).

And, as we all know, looking good in a suit is one of the main requirements to play 007, so Pattinson has already passed his first test as our newly-cast James Bond.

However you feel about "Tenet," one has to admit that its costumes are amazing and that Pattinson rocks every single outfit he wears. He carries himself with poise and class, playing the sidekick Neil to the film's protagonist, The Protagonist (John David Washington). Poise and class are the bedrocks on which James Bond is built, and Pattinson can certainly handle those qualities with skill.

"Tenet" is Nolan's lowest-rated directorial effort among critics on Rotten Tomatoes, and in his own review for /Film, Chris Evangelista pointed out that no one will be able to figure out what the heck is going on in the film. Having seen it, I agree and can confirm that I have trouble grasping the physics of its sci-fi rigmarole. The movie centers on a machine that can cause people and objects to travel through time in "reverse," yet they continue to exist in regular space. As a result, humans and items that have been "inverted" seem to be moving in reverse. To them, though, it's the rest of the world that appears to be going in the wrong direction.

Sources indicate that by the time-travel conceit of "Tenet," effect precedes cause. That means an inverted person can point a backward-moving gun at a target and, somehow, a bullet is sucked out of the wall and pulled back into the gun's chamber. How an inverted person caused that to happen is unclear to me. There is likewise a scene wherein the regular-moving Protagonist has to fight someone who is inverted and while Christopher Nolan's use of reverse photography is ingenious here, I couldn't help but wonder how one lands a punch when one is moving backward through time.

And if the time-travel physics are hard enough to fathom, there's also a twisted plot laid on top of them. The average sci-fi fan will likely be unable to remember all the details after just one go-through. Really, one will likely only recall a few fascinating visuals from "Tenet," and a very, very general sense of what's happening.

In short, Kenneth Branagh plays a dying Russian oligarch who has decided to destroy the world, with Robert Pattison and John David Washington playing the agents sent to foil his efforts. In addition, the oligarch's estranged wife (Elizabeth Debicki) is tragically mixed up in all this. The film even climaxes with armies of soldiers moving alternately forward and backward through time, and the apprehension of an oblique doomsday device. Truly, "Tenet" is a rather confusing movie.

Industry observers note that again, some of the imagery in "Tenet" is elaborate and fascinating, and the scenes of Neil and the Protagonist discussing things have a breezy tone. Even if their conversations are oblique and unmemorable, one gets the vibe that Pattinson is wholly at ease. He has a 007-like confidence.

Recent findings suggest that as mentioned, "Tenet" might be Christopher Nolan's least beloved film. It's too hard-to-follow to be a super crowd-pleaser, and it wasn't as well-loved by the Academy as some of Nolan's other movies (despite winning the Oscar for Best Visual Effects). Some critics were downright savage to the film, including Mick LaSalle. Writing for the San Francisco Chronicle, he gave the film one star out of four, arguing that it was confusing yet didn't really inspire a viewer to try to understand it.

In a recent development, brian Tallerico, writing for RogerEbert.com, was kinder, giving the film three stars out of four and drawing parallels to the James Bond franchise. He noted that Kenneth Branagh's destruction-hungry Russian oligarch is straight out of the Bond playbook, adding:.

"[T]here's never been a Bond movie so stuffed with expository dialogue. 'Tenet' spends roughly two hours of its 150-minute run time explaining what is happening, why it is happening, and what might happen next. And yet even with that it's still incredibly difficult to follow because Nolan goes so far down his own rabbit hole of time travel that one almost needs to take notes to keep up (and I still think it arguably wouldn't all add up if they could).".

Still, Tallerico noted, "If 'Tenet' can be a hard movie to engage with emotionally or even comprehend narratively, that doesn't take away from its craftsmanship on a technical level." It is, many might agree, an impressive feat, even if it is opaque.

Sources indicate that robert Pattinson, meanwhile, has remarked that "Tenet" is not about time travel. Of course not. As we now know, the movie is just as much about spy vibes and nice suits as it is time inversion.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • A few months ago, WABetaInfo reported that WhatsApp was working on its own backup service as an alternative to the current method of backing up chats, which relies on Apple’s iCloud.
  • At the time, the feature wasn’t available even to beta testers, but WABetaInfo’s report provided details on how it would work, including 2GB of free storage, optional paid plans for larger backups, and mandatory end-to-end encryption for backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Select WhatsApp beta testers on iOS are now seeing an option to use the app’s own backup service as an alternative to iCloud. Here are the details.

A few months ago, WABetaInfo reported that WhatsApp was working on its own backup service as an alternative to the current method of backing up chats, which relies on Apple’s iCloud.

At the time, the feature wasn’t available even to beta testers, but WABetaInfo’s report provided details on how it would work, including 2GB of free storage, optional paid plans for larger backups, and mandatory end-to-end encryption for backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers.

Now, the site reports that some WhatsApp people running the latest TestFlight build are seeing the option to switch from iCloud to WhatsApp’s own backup service, suggesting that a wider rollout may not be too far off.

Owners can switch to WhatsApp cloud storage from the Chat backup screen. Here, users will have to choose the backup provider they want to use. If they choose WhatsApp, they will have to secure their backups using end-to-end encryption. Since encryption is mandatory, users cannot skip this step. However, they can choose a different method to encrypt their backups. For example, users can secure their backups using a 64-digit encryption key. Users who do not know what to choose can opt for the passkey, which is the default method WhatsApp recommends. After users complete the setup, they can back up their chat history on WhatsApp’s servers. WhatsApp keeps the backup on its servers for four months after a subscription expires. If users do not renew their subscription, WhatsApp deletes the backup permanently.

Importantly, the site notes that backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers cannot presently be used to restore chats across platforms, meaning owners switching from iPhone to Android, or vice versa, will still need to rely on WhatsApp’s built-in chat transfer feature.

Although the feature appears to be rolling out to beta testers first, the report notes that “the latest version available on the App Store is also compatible with this functionality,” meaning WhatsApp could theoretically enable it for people running the public version without requiring another app enhancement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iFixit’s teardown of the new Apple HomeView is now up, revealing a device that seems nearly impossible to take apart and repair. Watch it below.

Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.

Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.

With heavily glued or adhesive-bonded components, including the display, speakers, antennas, and logic board, the teardown proved particularly challenging, even after the adhesive securing the display’s speakers was soaked in isopropyl alcohol.

At one point, one of them broke apart during removal, while the logic board required considerable force to separate from the chassis due to the thermal adhesive holding it in place.

It has been revealed that iFixit’s teardown covered the two HomeView variants: the tabletop model and the wall-mounted version. Interestingly, there are some internal differences between them, as the wall-mounted model has a slightly wider logic board to accommodate capacitors that are housed in the base of the tabletop version.

As a result, the wall-mounted HomeView also has smaller internal speakers, which helps explain the differences in their audio systems that Apple had already acknowledged at launch.

Back to the tabletop model, iFixit’s teardown also showed that separating the display from the base requires either specialized tools or extensive, potentially destructive disassembly of the display assembly, thanks to the way Apple routed the connecting cables through the pivot mechanism.

Once iFixit was in the base, however, there was some good news: the USB-C port is modular and relatively easy to access, as are the passive radiators and the board powering the lower assembly.

Still, an extremely short cable connecting the woofer to the board underneath made disassembly difficult, with iFixit questioning how anyone would be able to reconnect it during reassembly.

Percentage of Apple owners who are interested in repairing their device. 0.000001%.

Industry observers note that percentage of Apple owners who will actually try and repair their device. 0.00000001%.

Given all these repairability challenges, Shahram Mokhtari joked that while iFixit doesn’t have an official repairability scorecard for this category of device, he would give the Apple HomeView a “BEEP this thing” out of 10.

Sources indicate that han will shoot first in 70 mm IMAX when the original Star Wars returns to movie theaters next year. Lucasfilm and IMAX have confirmed that the 50th anniversary rerelease of Star Wars will be on the biggest screens possible next February, giving fans a strong reason to return to theaters.

In an official announcement on StarWars.com, Lucasfilm says Star Wars "will be shown across a select number of IMAX 70 mm film locations as well as playing in select theaters for a limited time.".

Recent findings suggest that that's not the only Star Wars release getting the deluxe IMAX treatment next year. Lucasfilm and IMAX reconfirmed that next year's stand-alone adventure Star Wars: Starfighter is also coming to the large-screen format. On May 28, 2027, Lucasfilm will release Star Wars: Starfighter, which was filmed for IMAX, shot with IMAX-certified film cameras, and converted to IMAX 70 mm film prints for release in a select number of IMAX film locations, according to an official announcement.

Star Wars: Starfighter is directed by Shawn Levy (Deadpool & Wolverine, Stranger Things) and stars Ryan Gosling (Blade Runner 2049, Barbie) as Kade Auberon, "a cynical rogue" who is "hurled into a dangerous adventure across the galaxy that puts him on a crash course with destiny." Starfighter also stars Matt Smith, Mia Goth, Aaron Pierre, Jamael Westman, Daniel Ings, Flynn Gray, and Amy Adams. The movie was written by Jonathan Tropper (Warrior, The Adam Project).

In a recent development, IMAX previously confirmed a 2027 release for the original Star Wars. It will be a rare opportunity to see George Lucas' 1977 science-fantasy epic that changed cinema without the alterations and digital effects that were added years after the fact.

In a recent development, lucas has become infamous for going back and tinkering with the edits and special effects throughout the original Star Wars trilogy. For the 20th anniversary of the franchise, Lucasfilm primed the pump for the release of Star Wars: The Phantom Menace with a monthly theatrical re-release of the Star Wars “Special Edition” trilogy, which saw robust changes and even additional scenes rendered with then-state-of-the-art computer graphics. Lucas continued to futz with Star Wars for the next three decades, which is how we wound up with the “Maclunkey Cut” of A Newly introduced Hope on Disney Plus.

It has been revealed that in 2025, former Lucasfilm boss Kathleen Kennedy teamed up with the British Film Institute to screen a print of Star Wars mentioned to be the earliest cut of the original that existed, untouched by its creator’s impulses to "perfect" it. The BFI even went an extra step in preparing the film reels for projection, finding an old, complete version of the original crawl, before "A New Hope" was added to the title, to run in front of the film.

After Lucasfilm teased intends to bring Star Wars back to theaters, longtime fans wondered which version of the film they'd get. Lucas himself had remarked that the original versions "will disappear" and, in his mind, the unaltered versions "[don't] really exist anymore." Fans who bemoan Lucas' additions and alterations to Star Wars have been resigned to relying on old VHS and Laserdisc copies, or pieced-together versions restored by fans, for decades now.

But soon, they'll have a chance to see the original on a brand-newly introduced scale — if they can get tickets.

Star Wars returns to movie theaters on Feb. 19, 2027.

It's a different kind of role for Mikkelsen, and a departure for his "Casino Royale" co-star Eva Green as well. Whereas she was glamorous and wounded as Vesper Lynd, she's just flat-out wounded as Morgan's serially abused sister-in-law.

Levring conjures the widescreen majesty of Sergio Leone (replete with an Ennio Morricone-esque score), and depicts the violence with a matter-of-fact bluntness. Alas, despite receiving mostly good reviews (it holds a 72% Fresh rating at Rotten Tomatoes), it got unceremoniously dumped into U.S. theaters in 2015. It's right now available to stream on multiple services, so now is the time to catch up with it!

Mikkelsen stars as Jon, who leaves Denmark with his brother Peter (Mikael Persbrandt) to start anew in America. Eventually, Jon's wife (Nanna Øland Fabricius) and son (Toke Lars Bjarke) join him, and the trio sets out on a stagecoach to begin the American chapter of their lives. Their hopes and dreams are immediately shattered when two criminals eject Jon from the stagecoach. The rape and kill his wife, and also murder his son.

In a recent development, jon tracks down the coach, and kills the two men. That's revenge served piping hot, but it causes newly introduced troubles for Jon, as one of the murderers was the brother of ruthless gang leader Henry Delarue (Morgan). Delarue flies into a rage and begins killing townspeople, hoping to intimidate them into helping him capture Jon. Delarue's savagery knows no bounds, and he's especially fond of inflicting his cruelty on Green's mute Madelaine.

Recent findings suggest that levring isn't out to reinvent the genre. He just wants to make a good-and-bloody Western where the truly nasty bad guys get theirs before the credits roll. If you're a fan of the genre, this is a solid programmer filled with superb performances. So saddle up and get your gunslinging fix. (And then catch up with one of Mikkelsen's finest performances in "The Hunt").

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The novel sold millions of copies, which meant a film adaptation was inevitable.
  • It has been revealed that "The Horse Whisperer" isn't quite on the level of the movie version of "The Bridges of Madison County" (a lovely film that Clint Eastwood saved from production limbo), but the screenplay credited to Eric Roth and Richard LaGravenese is nuanced in a way that maybe the novel isn't.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that nicholas Evans' "The Horse Whisperer" was a publishing phenomenon in 1995. The novel is about a young girl who's involved in a horseback riding accident that kills her best friend and their horse, leaving her and her own horse seriously injured. When she falls into a deep funk, her mother whisks her off to rural Montana. There, they try to heal her horse emotionally via a horse whisperer. And while she is married, the mother finds herself falling in love with the handsome, deeply sensitive animal shrink, something which, according to many critics, transformed the narrative into a shamelessly sentimental romance à la "The Bridges of Madison County.".

The novel sold millions of copies, which meant a film adaptation was inevitable. Like "The Bridges of Madison County," the pedigree didn't make it immediately attractive to A-list directors. But Robert Redford saw something more in the material and took it on as his first directorial effort since his brilliant 1994 drama "Quiz Show." For the first time in his filmmaking career, Redford took the lead in his own movie. He also assembled a sensationally talented cast that included Kristin Scott Thomas, Dianne Wiest, Sam Neill, Chris Cooper, and Cherry Jones. For the role of the young girl, he and the casting team of Ellen Chenoweth and Gretchen Rennell went with up-and-comer Scarlett Johansson, who gave a moving performance that wound up being her breakthrough role.

It has been revealed that "The Horse Whisperer" isn't quite on the level of the movie version of "The Bridges of Madison County" (a lovely film that Clint Eastwood saved from production limbo), but the screenplay credited to Eric Roth and Richard LaGravenese is nuanced in a way that maybe the novel isn't. And though it's not one of Redford's best movies, it's a strong piece of work that deserves more attention.

In a recent development, "The Horse Whisperer" holds a 72% Fresh critical approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and grossed $187 million at the worldwide box office upon hitting theaters. That was a decent result for Touchstone Pictures, but it didn't come close to matching the runaway success of its source material.

Robert Redford rarely failed to strike up chemistry with his leading ladies ("The Great Gatsby" being a notable exception), so it's hardly a shocker that he's perfectly paired with Kristin Scott Thomas. This is not, however, a heated attraction, as Redford's character is still mourning the end of a previous romance where the woman chose the city over him and the country. Thomas is from the city, too (and, again, married), so he's worried that another heartbreak is around the corner.

As for Scarlett Johansson, she captures the grief of a young woman whose life has been irreparably changed. Her leg was partially amputated, which she fears will make her undesirable to romantic partners as she gets older. This gives rise to the most overpoweringly emotional scene in the movie when, after a row with her mother, Johansson's character tearfully asks, "Who's going to want me?" If that doesn't switch on your waterworks, go straight to the doctor, because your heart isn't properly functioning.

Industry observers note that "The Horse Whisperer" is available to rent via streaming, but the film is badly in need of a digital restoration. Hopefully, Disney will commission one at some point, although I'm not sure if the movie is a popular enough library title to merit such treatment.

34 Years Later, the Best 'Far Side' Quote Will Still Leave You Speechless

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (856 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that in recent months, I’ve been examining the best-ever quotes from various newspaper comic strips, and in that time I’ve determined that every comic strip requires its own approach.
  • Larson didn’t do deep and inspirational.
  • Larson’s work often requires the reader to investigate something, but usually not in any kind of overly deep way.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in recent months, I’ve been examining the best-ever quotes from various newspaper comic strips, and in that time I’ve determined that every comic strip requires its own approach. For Charles Schulz’s Peanuts, I chose something heartfelt and inspirational because those comics and characters really have inspired people. For Bill Watterson’s Calvin and Hobbes, I investigated something more philosophical, as the best of those comics make the audience contemplate human nature and the world around them. But for Gary Larson’s The Far Side, the task is monumentally different.

Larson didn’t do deep and inspirational. Many of his cartoons required you to think, but not because they were thoughtful. Larson’s work was brilliant, and it sometimes took a few minutes to figure out what the punchline was. Take, this comic strip where an artist is painting a woman as a half-fly creature, for example. You likely see the woman or the painting first, and you wonder why the artist is painting her that way. Only after inspecting the comic more closely do you see the dead fly stuck to his glasses.

Larson’s work often requires the reader to investigate something, but usually not in any kind of overly deep way.

It has been revealed that the Far Side is brilliant, but it's not the kind of comic strip that makes you ponder life’s significant questions. Larson channeled his genius into joke-telling, and that’s what made The Far Side so sharply funny. As such, determining Larson’s best-ever Far Side quote shouldn’t be some insightful, inspirational, or thoughtful journey — even though I did try going that way at first.

According to recent reports, I thought maybe the quote should come from a comic about God, as several Far Side comics feature God as a character. But after reading a bunch of Larson’s God comics, I determined that God actually isn’t all that deep or interesting. Sometimes he’s just kind of a jerk.

According to recent reports, then I thought to look up comics about death, thinking that maybe Larson had something profound to say on the subject. Given Larson’s signature macabre style of humor, death is featured frequently in The Far Side, but nothing seemed all that weighty or important. I finally abandoned this approach when I found a comic where a snake hanged himself with his own body.

That’s when I gave up on going deep and decided to just find something funny. But there are thousands of Far Side comics, and Larson’s humor varied. Sometimes he was dark, sometimes he was silly, sometimes he deconstructed a well-known saying or song or other pop culture reference. So I tried to find a quote that did all — or at least most of — what Larson was known for. Also, I wanted a quote where the visual wasn’t required to get the joke. Larson’s work was highly visual, and with generally just one panel, it often had the visual as the setup and the caption as the punchline. If I was looking for the best ever Far Side comic, it would be one where the visual and the caption work in concert. But while trying to find the best-ever quote, I wanted something where the image was not required.

Industry observers note that for a little while I thought about going with “Welcome to hell… here’s your accordion,” from a comic which indicates Heaven and Hell. In Heaven, you’re given a harp, but in Hell you’re given an accordion. I liked this because it’s very dark and silly, and it’s the kind of thing you’d only find in The Far Side. Eventually though I softened on it because the visual is still the stronger element in this one. The line comes off as basically a funny non-sequitur without the visual. To get the whole joke about how accordions are terrible instruments, you really need the contrast.

According to recent reports, after abandoning that comic, I found this one from 1992 and realized it was the perfect fit. The image shows a mime under a falling tree and the caption reads:.

“Question: If a tree falls in the forest and no one’s around, and it hits a mime, does anyone care?”.

It has been revealed that I think this is the one because it’s funny, because it's dark, because it's silly, and because it takes a well-known idiom — the tree falling in the woods question — and turns it into a punchline. That may not do everything that Larson did, but it’s a lot of his very best qualities all in one place.

In a recent development, and, unlike the vast majority of Far Side comics, it’s more about the words than the image. Larson’s gags were almost always visual, or at least relied on a visual component to get his jokes across. For this comic, I’d argue that you don’t need the visual at all. Sure, the drawing is funny, but in no way is it required. Also, this quote is entirely lacking in emotional or philosophical depth, which is precisely what you want when you’re reading The Far Side.
