📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Todd Boehly gave an insight into his no nonsense approach to investing in sports and entertainment in the concluding fireside chat of the Qatar Film Committee’s Doha Industry Days over the weekend.
  • The billionaire investor’s holding organization Eldridge has some $75B in assets including stakes in Backrooms distributor A24, and Fulwell Entertainment as well as the Los Angeles Lakers, the Los Angeles Sparks, the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Trent Rockets among many more.
  • Industry observers note that the holding is also a partner with Deadline owner Penske Media in the Penske Media Eldridge unit encompassing live TV entertainment specialist Dick Clark Productions as well as events such as the Golden Globes and SXSW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Todd Boehly gave an insight into his no nonsense approach to investing in sports and entertainment in the concluding fireside chat of the Qatar Film Committee’s Doha Industry Days over the weekend.

The billionaire investor’s holding organization Eldridge has some $75B in assets including stakes in Backrooms distributor A24, and Fulwell Entertainment as well as the Los Angeles Lakers, the Los Angeles Sparks, the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Trent Rockets among many more.

Industry observers note that the holding is also a partner with Deadline owner Penske Media in the Penske Media Eldridge unit encompassing live TV entertainment specialist Dick Clark Productions as well as events such as the Golden Globes and SXSW. Related Stories News Joe Russo Talks 'Doomsday' Teaser-Trailer Strategy Ahead Of Rumored Monday Drop: "I Have To interact With Fans" News Watermelon Expands Production Ambitions As It Seals Partnership With Qatar's Film Committee.

Boehly first connected with A24 cofounder Daniel Katz, when the latter headed Guggenheim Partners’ film finance group in New York, while he was president of the global investment firm before leaving to create Eldridge. Watch on Deadline.

“One of the things I believe is that there’s very few entertainment people that understand math… the math of entertainment is really about understanding how are you taking risk and then how are you distributing risk,” he mentioned in the chat entitled “Playing to Win”.

“It’s no different than any other industry, if you’re thinking about what amount of risk you are willing to take and then how are you going to feed that risk,” he added.

Boehly remarked Katz had impressed him from the start for his ability to identify and work with risk during his time with Guggenheim Partners.

“Daniel’s real magic, when he worked on our trading floor from, let’s call it like 2008 to 2012, he didn’t take a lot of risks, but he said ‘no’ a lot,” he said.

It has been revealed that “There was a slate that was done by a group called Stark Investments, and one of their big films was Poseidon. I remember it indicated up on our desk. And Daniel was immediately like, this is a disaster. It’s going to cost so much money, you know, they’re not going to be able to make any return on it.”.

The $160M disaster movie by Wolfgang Petersen went down in film financing folklore after it faltered at the box office and failed to gross enough to cover its P&A costs.

According to recent reports, boehly provided $19M in seed money for A24 as Katz launched the manufacturer in 2012 with David Fenkel and Joh Hodges. It was last publicly valued at $3.5 billion in June 2024.

Sources indicate that “Everyone told me in Hollywood that there’s no room for another distribution organization,” recalled the businessman. “His early successes with Spring Breakers and The Bling Ring were really structured finance trades.”.

“You’re not really allowed to talk about that in the entertainment world because everything’s creative and creator driven… what Daniel was really good at, because he sat on a trading desk and he understood risk and he understood math, he was really good at figuring out how am I going to get my money back using different windows.”.

Starring James Franco, Selena Gomez, Vanessa Hudgens, Harmony Korine’s Spring Breakers premiered in competition in Venice and went on to gross $31M.

“Spring Breakers cost a couple million bucks to buy, and he ended up making 10 million bucks or so very quickly on, because he really understood that it’s a structured finance straight,” said Boehly.

He added that beyond Katz’s business savviness, the firm had also understood how to tap into social media to generate audience engagement as well as how to plug into trends of the moment.

Sources indicate that “One of the things that A24 has done an amazing job at is being able to read the cultural zeitgeist. I think Civil War was really well timed; Marty Supreme was very well timed with Timothée Chalamet and his ascension as probably one of the top actors for the next couple of decades.”.

Boehly also highlighted A24’s strategy of growing a cohort of directors and actors, who returned to work with the organization on a regular basis.

“He wants repeat customers. He wants the directors coming back… he wants the actors coming back… because then it’s not a transaction, it becomes a recurring business with enterprise,” said Boehly.

“So many people think about the film business, ‘Oh, it’s a transaction’. But if you’re really thinking about how to build an enterprise, then you need to make sure that you have a recurring revenue base. And the way you do that in this industry is you get repeat users.”.

He also gave insight into how Katz constructs A24’s slate in a way that enables it to work with established names and newcomers and turn a profit, suggesting that over a portfolio of 15 films, nine would be “the core bread and butter”.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s a budget of 25 to 40 million bucks. It’s the expectation that he’s going to make 1.35 times,” he explained. “And if you think about the math of it again, you get 0.8 times your money back right away or very promptly. So, when you think about the risk that you have, you’re in for 0.2. If you make 1.35 and your risk capital is 0.2, but you’re going to make six, seven times that 0.2.”.

It has been revealed that “And then he’ll take three big swings and make something that has the capacity to become multiple films out of the content… he’ll take 1.2 times. So, he’ll modify his expectations on the rate of return to achieve something that might have more enterprise value or longevity on the back of it.”.

Boehly suggested the final three films would be by up-and-coming young directors, and would require time, energy and effort rather than major financial investments and risk.

“He’s always thinking about how do I build that portfolio in order to have my bread and butter, have the opportunity to have something that’s got longevity and then find someone who’s going to be special in the industry,” he remarked.

Latest Update: UK court rules Apple can share the top secret order everyone already knew

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (754 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.
  • Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the matter ….
  • Recent findings suggest that the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.

Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the matter ….

Recent findings suggest that the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022. This extended end-to-end encryption to almost all your iCloud data, meaning Apple has no access, and therefore cannot grant access to any government agencies who come knocking on its door.

Industry observers note that the feature is off by default because it means Apple cannot help you access any of your data if, for example, you forget your iCloud password. However, those who want to maximize the privacy of their iCloud account can enable it.

In 2025, the British government ordered Apple to create a backdoor to allow access by security services and law enforcement. Even worse, the order was issued under legislation that prohibits companies from revealing that they have received this demand.

In a recent development, this would have meant that British customers who enabled ADP would think that their data was safe when in fact it wasn’t. As we’ve said many times before, any backdoor created for use by the good guys is vulnerable to discovery and exploitation by the bad guys.

Sources indicate that it would have been illegal for Apple to reveal that it had been instructed to compromise the privacy of customer data, but the company found a clever way to effectively communicate this without breaking the law. Apple declared it was withdrawing ADP from the UK without explaining its reason.

“Apple can no longer offer Advanced Data Protection (ADP) in the United Kingdom to upcoming users and current UK users will eventually need to disable this security feature. ADP protects iCloud data with end-to-end encryption, which means the data can only be decrypted by the user who owns it, and only on their trusted devices. We are gravely disappointed that the protections provided by ADP will not be available to our customers in the UK […] As we have said many times before, we have never built a backdoor or master key to any of our products or services and we never will.”.

Tell me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP without telling me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP ….

At this point, it was an open secret. However, ridiculously, despite the fact that everyone in the security and privacy field knew about it and was talking about it, Apple was still not allowed to officially confirm it.

According to recent reports, the iPhone maker asked the Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) to allow it to openly discuss the order, with privacy campaigners backing this call. The Financial Times reports that the court has now ruled in Apple’s favor.

The UK government must admit that it issued a secret order to Apple to allow it access to encrypted customer data, a court has ruled […] The Home Office has “not established that it would be damaging to national security” to reveal that Apple had received a “technical capability notice” (TCN), the tribunal said. The ruling means that […] “much” of Apple and the non-profits’ legal challenge can now take place in open court.

One of the great ironies is that most people had never heard of ADP until the government effectively made it headline news in the tech press three years after it launched – a classic example of the Streisand Effect.

It has been revealed that this ruling is a win both for transparency and commonsense. To be clear, the actual requirement for a backdoor remains in place, but this can now be challenged in open court.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday isn't until Nov. 27, but the early Black Friday sales are in full swing. I've been keeping an eye on all the best fitness trackers and smartwatch deals so that you can snag the best possible price from now until the end of Cyber Monday (Nov. 30). Whether you want a full-featured fitness smartwatch or a more recovery-focused tracker, here are the discounts you can find right now, including on brands like Apple, Oura, Garmin, and more.

According to recent reports, the Oura Ring 5 is at its lowest ever price: $299 for black and silver, $399 for all other colors. These are the lowest prices ever for these rings, which usually go for $399 and $499, respectively. The Oura Ring 5 is the smallest and most comfortable smart ring I've tried, although it's worth noting it requires a $5.99/month subscription fee.

For an even cheaper deal, the older Oura Ring 4 is $249—a full $100 off its list price of $349. If you opt for "stealth" (matte black), the price is $279; for gold, it's $286.61, down from $399. While this model has since been replaced by the Oura Ring 5, it's still an accurate and comfortable smart ring—especially if tracking your sleep is your priority.

Whoop may be one of the most expensive smart bands out there, thanks to its subscription-only model. But that price is particularly low right now, since the Peak membership that normally goes for $239 is now $199. Peak is the middle tier, and it's the one I recommend. While you can get Whoop One for $189 in this sale, the $10 you save isn't really worth it given the features you'd be missing. I also wouldn't normally recommend Whoop Life, since its ECG readings and blood pressure estimates aren't really worth the extra $100+. That said, if you do want it, the Life tier is $299 right now instead of $359.

The new Luna band is on sale for $119.20, down from a normal price of $149. The Luna band is made by Indian smartwatch manufacturer Noise, the same company behind the Luna Ring that I reviewed last year. The ring is no longer available in the U.S., but the band is. It's a Whoop-style screenless fitness tracker, potentially a worthy competitor to the Fitbit Air and other smart bands.

This is the brand-new Apple Watch model, and it's actually worth the upgrade. One of the biggest reasons is that the Series 12's new processor (called, confusingly, the S11 chip) supports some features older Apple Watches can't, and a good rule of thumb is that whenever there's a break in software compatibility, it makes sense to get the newer model. Right now, I'm seeing it for as low as $329, down from the list price of $399. (And if you're stuck deciding between an Apple Watch and a Fitbit, Beth breaks it all down in her comparison of the two watches.).

It has been revealed that the CMF Watch 3 Pro is Nothing's latest smartwatch, and it incorporates AI features powered by ChatGPT; you can at the moment pick it up at a major discount. Originally $99, you can get the CMF Watch 3 Pro for $55. This is the lowest price this smartwatch has been.

If you're looking specifically for a sporty, outdoors watch, Garmin sets the standard. (You could definitely call me something of a Garmin enthusiast.) Here are the best Black Friday deals on Garmin watches that I've seen so far:.

Sources indicate that the 44mm Garmin Instinct 3 is 249.99 (down from $449.99). The 1.2-inch color AMOLED display makes the screen more readable in bright daylight conditions, and battery life is best-in-class—a must for those going off-grid.

The Garmin Fēnix 8 in titanium with a gray band is $749.99 (down from $999.99). While this is last year's model, it's a perfectly solid option if you don't specifically need the titanium case or the latest mapping engine in the latest Fenix 9 Pro.

The Garmin Forerunner 265 is $299.99 (down from $449.99). Although it isn't the latest and greatest anymore, this is still a fan favorite among Garmin users. It's a step above entry-level options, with dual-band GPS, power meter compatibility, and advanced analytics (like training status).

Industry observers note that these aren't the only sales you'll see on fitness watches and trackers during the big shopping holiday; the following brands have announced they'll be launching more deals on Nov. 19:.

Oura (specifically, the Oura Ring 5).

Additionally, though the sale has ended, the Google Pixel Watch 5 was recently marked down by $100; I'll be keeping an eye on this device to see if that particular deal comes back once Black Friday officially arrives.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

According to recent reports, the best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

According to recent reports, for most people, the Apple Watch SE 3 at $199 is a good starting point, covering everyday fitness tracking, notifications, and essential health features without the higher price of the Series 12. If you want more advanced health monitoring and a more premium smartwatch experience, the Series 12 at $329 is worth considering.

Yes, Garmin is one of the best brands when it comes to rugged sports watches and fitness trackers. The Forerunner line especially, is a go-to pick for accurate and reliable GPS tracking for runners.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After surviving the Upside Down, Noah Schnapp apparently volunteered as tribute for the latest Hunger Games film.

Marking the opening weekend of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, the Stranger Things alum revealed that he auditioned to play Haymitch with a selfie in a blonde wig, admitting that Joseph Zada was the right choice.

In a recent development, “POV: my audition for Haymitch,” wrote Schnapp on his Instagram Story with some laughing emojis. “@josephzada think they picked right for this one.”.

Now playing in theaters, the Hunger Games prequel from director Francis Lawrence and writers Billy Ray and Michael Lesslie is based on Suzanne Collins’ 2025 novel Sunrise on the Reaping, set during Haymitch’s game in the Second Quarter Quell.

Recent findings suggest that starring Zada as Haymitch, Sunrise on the Reaping is set 24 years before 2012’s The Hunger Games, in which Woody Harrelson originated the role. It follows 2023’s The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes in continuity, set 40 years later. Watch on Deadline.

The movie also stars Elle Fanning, McKenna Grace, Ben Wang, Jesse Plemons, Glenn Close, Billy Porter, Maya Hawke, Kieran Culkin, Kelvin Harrison Jr., Lili Taylor and Ralph Fiennes.
